The low reticulocyte count indicates bone marrow failure rather than hemolysis, which strongly points toward Diamond-Blackfan Anemia given the macrocytosis and anemia in an infant. Does the infant have any physical anomalies such as thumb abnormalities, facial dysmorphism, or short stature?

The normal adenosine deaminase and B-cell results effectively rule out Severe Combined Immunodeficiency. Given the macrocytic anemia, low reticulocyte count, and absence of other cytopenias, Diamond-Blackfan Anemia remains the leading diagnosis.
